evidence.quote: No doubt, too, that even his restless-minded, introspective, self-conscious children who knew him best were much too ignorant of the world
was not maintained by nature without a sacrifice of the qualities which would have upset it. The world never loved perfect poise.

adjudications.reason: The plan's risks name the 'No doubt...' hedges as the passage most exposed to over-compression. The revision keeps only the first hedge, then jumps straight to the aphorism. The cut sentence is the old man's self-indictment: the children were too ignorant to see the model before them. 'A coarser instrument' then sets up 'The world never loved perfect poise.' Without them the passage reads closer to eulogy. 'They abused Charles Francis for his judgment' is a lesser loss and is not restored, to limit word growth.

evidence.quote: So they were. He could not be convinced that moral standards had nothing to do with it
better than those of his successors. So they were. Nature had given to the boy Henry a character

adjudications.reason: The voice profile calls for periodic sentences ending in a dry reversal. In the source, 'So they were' is answered at once: the Puritan was right about his standards and wrong that standards mattered. The revision cuts that answer, so 'So they were' becomes plain agreement, and the old nature's resistance to change loses its stated cause.

evidence.quote: In politics it was the old Ciceronian idea of government by the best that produced the long line of New England statesmen.
With this bargain Mr. Adams and his statesman friends would have nothing to do

adjudications.reason: The essentials, government 'by the best' and the Webster succession, survive in paragraph 14. Paragraph 15's 'this sort of world' still resolves to that system. In chapter 005, 'his statesman friends' and their refusal of the bargain read clearly without this setup. Restoring it would be an improvement, not a necessary repair, and the word budget is already exceeded by the confirmed repairs.

evidence.quote: to write dull discussions in the newspapers, to try to be dull in some different way from that of his great-grandfather

adjudications.reason: The pair is still recoverable. The sentence just before sets the newspaper discussions against 'that of his great-grandfather,' and the paragraph names both the newspaper and John Adams's Works. 'The one... the other' therefore reads naturally as that pair.

evidence.quote: he set up a party of his own.
during the next five or six years, his father alone counted for much

adjudications.reason: Paragraph 9 ends 'he set up a party of his own,' and paragraph 10 opens on that party's members, so the causal link is immediate. The chapter title supplies the 1848–1854 span, and paragraph 6 says 'during the next five or six years, his father alone counted for much.'

remaining_concerns: The two necessary repairs add about 73 words, against a target of about +19, leaving the chapter roughly 50 words (≈1.8%) over 3000. No remaining material is listed as optional, and further cuts would hit essentials or protected passages, so the overage is accepted rather than sacrificing meaning.
Restoring 'Sumner aspired to break the succession, but not the system' and 'statesmen, not politicians' (F3) would strengthen the setup for chapter 005, if a later pass finds room.

replacements.new: which would have upset it. No doubt, too, that even his restless-minded, introspective, self-conscious children who knew him best were much too ignorant of the world and of human nature to suspect how rare and complete was the model before their eyes. A coarser instrument would have impressed them more. The world never loved perfect poise.

replacements.reason: Restores the source's second 'No doubt' hedge and the transition into V3, per the plan's stated risk.
